newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Tajikistan's hunt for maverick warlord said over.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan's hunt for maverick warlord said over.

text.p: The Tajik government appeared on Monday to give up hope of catching maverick warlord Rizvon Sadirov, saying an operation to hunt down the armed leader was over though he remained on the run.

"Government forces along with units of the (Islamic) opposition yesterday completed their operation against Rizvon Sadirov's group," Zafar Saidov, spokesman for Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov, told Reuters by telephone from the Tajik capital Dushanbe.

"Rizvon, his wounded brother Fatkhudin and two others are still hiding in the mountains," Saidov added. He said they were located somewhere along the Krasny mountain range, 80 km (50 miles) east of Dushanbe.
Sadirov's group, who once fought for the Islamic opposition but whose loyalties are now far from clear, took several foreigners hostage in December.

In a complicated scenario, Sadirov was also involved in taking 14 foreign aid workers, military observers and journalists hostage for two weeks in February, demanding his group be allowed free passage back to the republic from a base in neighbouring Afghanistan.

Saidov said the government and its former Islamic opposition foes -- the two sides signed a ceasefire in December to try and end a bloody four-year civil war -- had killed at least 15 of Sadirov's band during the 10-day operation and captured 24.
Sadirov's group was estimated by the government to number about 45.
The beleaguered Tajik government is struggling to retain a grip on the former Soviet republic which is awash with arms and subject to bitter factional rivalries.
